description: Create an analytics dashboard. Only `title` is required — source defaults to the whole workspace and dateRange to last30days. Add widgets by listing their types (the MCP assigns ids and lays them out automatically), scope with source ({type:"folders",folderIds} | {type:"team"} | {type:"workspace"}) and dateRange ({preset}), and optionally group widgets into sections. Design guidance: lead with a narrative widget as the first widget; group sections by the QUESTION they answer, not by widget type; don't pad — every widget earns its place (aim for 4-16 widgets on a full build); if something can't be expressed by the widget catalog, put it in a narrative widget's focus instead of faking it. Call list_dashboard_widgets first for the widget catalog, config vocabulary, design rules, and full examples. Creating a dashboard does not share it publicly; only share_dashboard creates a public link. If settings.feedback.sheetWebhookUrl is set, each Feedback submission made on the shared dashboard is posted to that external Google Apps Script URL. Shared dashboard links cache widget data, so field and media edits can take up to about 5 minutes to show for date ranges that include today (15 at most) and up to about 17 minutes for past ranges (60 at most); any dashboard update refreshes it at once. Viewer settings (the settings input): Do not pass settings unless the user explicitly asks to change this dashboard's viewer settings. Saving fields, feedback or fieldEdits moves that dashboard onto the settings flow immediately: its media pages use these groups and this Feedback setup from then on. Each section (fields, feedback, fieldEdits, labels, comments, profiles) replaces that whole section when sent; a section left out keeps its saved value. Call get_dashboard first and resend every key of the section you change; a key left out resets to its default. Get field ids from list_fields. Ids that are not the company's fields are dropped when saving and returned in droppedFieldIds. When feedback.isEnabled is true, pass a non-empty feedback.fieldIds (score fields) rather than leaving it empty. Only set feedback.sheetWebhookUrl when the user gives the Apps Script URL. fieldEdits.fieldIds may list only fields that have allowed values (the server rejects any other field with a 400) and that the dashboard's media pages show; pass an empty fieldIds to turn field editing off. Labels and comments on the shared link are off until the user asks to turn them on. Mode 'apply' (labels) or 'reply' (comments) lets a link viewer write as one of the dashboard's feedback submitter names (feedback.submitters, even while feedback itself is off), or as another typed name only when feedback.allowOtherSubmitter is true. Anyone holding the share link can pick any of those names, because the link has no sign-in (an accepted risk; every entry is marked as made via this dashboard), so confirm the names with the user before saving a write mode. With no submitter names nobody can write. Label groups that are not active refuse the whole save with a 400 rather than being dropped. Saving only settings.profiles does not move media pages onto the settings flow. settings.profiles is a list of up to 5 groups, one per custom field (a field may appear only once), each with a label (for example Speakers or Products) and entries that give a value of that field a name, image, description and link. Entry names must equal that field's values (trim, case-insensitive), and a name or id listed twice in a group is rejected with a 400; they are matched by display string, so renaming a value in the media fields orphans its profile. Names, descriptions, links and images are PUBLIC to anyone with the dashboard link: write plain text only, no HTML, and confirm the descriptions and links with the user before saving. This MCP cannot upload images: leave imageKey out, or pass one copied unchanged from get_dashboard. To add an image over the API, POST it (multipart, JPEG/PNG/WEBP/GIF, max 2 MB) to /v1/dashboards/:dashboardId/profile-image and use the returned imageKey.

assignTo.description: User ids, or group ids in the "<groupId> (G)" convention, to share view access with

dateRange.description: Date range — strict preset only, no free-form start/end dates

preset.description: One of: last7days | last30days | last3months | yearToDate | allTime

filters.description: Fixed pre-filter applied to every widget on the dashboard (not a filter bar viewers can change). filters.filterList is an array of { fieldName: field id, fieldOperator: "include", fieldValue: string[] (1 or more), fieldCondition? }; a media file shows only when that field holds one of the values. Shared links apply include filters only. Other keys pass through but only filterList is enforced.

fieldName.description: Field `id` from list_fields or create_field (12 characters), never the database `_id`

isDefault.description: Make this the owner's default dashboard. Setting true clears the default flag on the owner's other dashboards

sections.description: Optional named widget groups (tabs). Each references widgets by their explicit ids; widgets in no section form the implicit Overview group.

icon.description: Kebab-case lucide icon name. Known good: "dollar-sign", "globe", "users", "trending-up", "message-square", "star", "target", "calendar", "chart-line", "circle-play", "circle-check", "circle-alert". Lucide renamed its "<thing>-circle" icons to "circle-<thing>" (use "circle-play", not "play-circle"); an unknown name shows a blank dot.

widgetIds.description: Widget ids in this section — must match explicit `id`s set on widgets[]

settings.description: Viewer settings for media pages opened from this dashboard's share link: which fields show, how the Fields tab groups them, the Feedback button, which fields Feedback submitters may edit, labels and comments with the reviewer names (feedback submitters) who may write them, and profile groups. Anyone holding the share link can pick any of those names, because the link has no sign-in (an accepted risk; every entry is marked as made via this dashboard), so confirm the names with the user before saving a write mode. With no submitter names nobody can write. Label groups that are not active refuse the whole save with a 400 rather than being dropped. Saving only settings.profiles does not move media pages onto the settings flow. settings.profiles is a list of up to 5 groups, one per custom field (a field may appear only once), each with a label (for example Speakers or Products) and entries that give a value of that field a name, image, description and link. isEnabled.description: Show comments on media pages opened from this shared dashboard

mode.description: 'view' shows comments read-only; 'reply' also lets a viewer, as a reviewer name, comment and reply

allowOtherSubmitter.description: Lets a reviewer type a name that is not in submitters.

fieldIds.description: Fields a reviewer gives feedback on. Empty means every field the media page shows.

fieldRules.description: Per feedback field: a short row label and the allowed score range, used for both the reviewer's score and the approver's score.

groups.description: Pills in the Feedback dialog, each listing feedback field ids in order. Leave out to reuse fields.groups.

isEnabled.description: Show the Feedback button on media pages opened from this shared dashboard

removeReasons.description: Reasons for removing a call from scoring. Empty hides that option.

reviewScope.description: 'dashboard' (default) lists and reviews only this dashboard's feedback; 'company' lists every dashboard's feedback in the company. Use 'company' only on a manager dashboard, never on a personal one.

sheetWebhookUrl.description: External Google Apps Script web app URL. Speak posts one row per Feedback submission (call date, media link, scores, submitter name, notes) to it. Only https://script.google.com/macros/s/<id>/exec addresses are called; other values are saved but never called. Never shown to viewers.

submitters.description: Names a reviewer picks from. Empty lets them type their own name.

fieldIds.description: Custom fields that people on the Feedback name list (feedback.submitters, with allowOtherSubmitter) may edit in an "Edit fields" tab on media pages opened from this shared dashboard, in tab order. Only fields that have allowed values (others return a 400) and that the media page shows (fields.includeIds, or the company's public fields when it is empty); others are ignored on the page. Max 50 unique ids. Empty turns field editing off.

groups.description: Pills on the media page Fields tab, each listing the field ids it shows. Empty means no pills.

includeIds.description: Field ids a viewer sees on each media page opened from this shared dashboard, in this order. Private fields are shown when listed. Empty shows only the company's public fields.

orderIds.description: Used only when includeIds is empty: these fields show first, in this order, then every other public field. Does not change which fields are visible.

isEnabled.description: Show labels on media pages opened from this shared dashboard

labelGroupIds.description: Label groups the link shows and offers (unique, at most 100). Empty means every active label. Get group ids from list_labels (items with isGroup true).

mode.description: 'view' shows labels read-only; 'apply' also lets a viewer, as a reviewer name, add and remove labels

profiles.description: Profile groups (up to 5, one per field) shown on the shared dashboard. Replaces the whole list when sent; an empty list removes every group. Public to anyone with the link; plain text only.

entries.description: Up to 60 entries. Empty removes every entry of the group.

description.description: Plain-text description, max 600 chars, no HTML. Public to anyone with the dashboard link.

id.description: Entry id (lowercase slug, unique in the group); leave out for a new entry and the server generates one

imageKey.description: S3 URI of an image in Speak's own bucket, set by the in-app image upload. Only pass a value copied from get_dashboard; this MCP cannot upload images.

link.description: Optional http or https URL, max 2048 chars. Public to anyone with the dashboard link.

name.description: Entry name, 1-80 chars; must equal a value of the group's field (trim, case-insensitive) and be unique within the group

fieldId.description: Custom field id whose values the entries describe (from list_fields); each field at most once

imageShape.description: How entry images are cropped: round or square

label.description: Group label shown on the dashboard, 1-40 chars (for example Speakers)

folderIds.description: Folder ids (1-250) — required when type is "folders", forbidden otherwise

type.description: folders = specific folder ids; team = the caller's team scope; workspace = everything accessible

title.description: Dashboard name, max 60 chars (the only required field)

widgets.description: Widgets to place on the dashboard, in order (max 24). The MCP assigns ids and computes a tidy two-per-row grid layout matching the Speak UI unless you pass explicit id/layout.

binding.description: Per-widget scope override: { source?, dateRange?: {preset}, filter? }. Omit any key to inherit the dashboard's value.

config.description: Per-type config (STRICT — unknown keys are rejected). metric-chart: mark (line|bar|area|donut|stacked-bar) + metric + groupBy/series + thresholds; table: rowsAre + columns [{header, field|metric}] (+ display: cards and card for session cards); stat-cards: tiles; field-distribution: fieldName+measure+chartType (required); narrative: focus; notes: content (+ actions for buttons); chat-history: limit (optional, past conversations to list, 1-100, default 25). Call list_dashboard_widgets for the full per-type vocabulary + metric/filter grammar. Omit for a sensible valid default (except field-distribution, which needs fieldName).

id.description: Optional explicit widget id (kebab-case). Required if you reference the widget from sections[].widgetIds; auto-generated otherwise.

layout.description: Explicit 12-column grid position. Omit to auto-place two-per-row like the UI. Widgets must not overlap within a section group.

title.description: Widget title, max 40 chars (defaults to a per-type label)

type.description: Widget type: narrative | stat-cards | metric-chart | table | comparison | field-distribution | sentiment-trend | themes | people | team-activity | notes | chat-history
